claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy contains BCC/B2 and FCC phases.
The initial microstructure consists of continuous, planar dual-phase lamellae.
Low tensile ductility in the initial alloy is caused by catastrophic cracking at phase interfaces.
Severe plastic deformation at 600–750 °C will induce dynamic recrystallization.
Severe plastic deformation at 600–750 °C will fragment the lamellae.
Aging at 300–400 °C for 1–4 hours will stabilize the patterned interfaces without causing coarsening.
The treatment will convert continuous planar interfaces into curved, discontinuous, interconnected lamellar segments.
The treated structure will contain high-angle grain boundaries and a network of dislocation cells.
High-angle grain boundaries, curved lamellae, and dislocation-cell structures will impede crack propagation.
The patterned microstructure will redistribute strain and promote more uniform plasticity.
Severe-deformation shear stress will break continuous lamellar connectivity and produce zig-zag or curved interfaces.
Curved or zig-zag interfaces will reduce the effective stress-intensity factor at interface tips relative to planar interfaces.
Aging will stabilize a high density of deformation-induced defects and refine the phase distribution.
Dislocation pile-up relaxation and shear-band multiplication will promote a transition from interfacial brittle fracture to transgranular or mixed-mode fracture.
Grain-boundary sliding and localized shear banding will promote uniform plasticity during room-temperature tension.
The proposed treatment will increase uniform elongation by more than 50%.
The proposed treatment will maintain or slightly increase yield strength through grain refinement and interface strengthening.
The untreated or conventionally annealed baseline has tensile elongation below 5% and initiates failure at phase interfaces.
Temperatures above 0.6 Tm will cause patterned-structure coarsening, while strains below 2 will leave lamellar continuity intact.
